question: I'm an IS sophomore (P-013) on academic warning, currently enrolled in 3 courses (36 units) in Spring 2026. If I withdraw from one 9-unit course, what happens to my academic status?

domain_contributions.policies: Withdrawn courses receive W grade (non-factorable, does not affect QPA) but still count toward semester units. Going below 36 units (full-time threshold) without Dean approval triggers additional consequences. AW students already face heightened scrutiny.
domain_contributions.courses: Starting at 36 units; withdrawing 9 units → 27 units remaining = below full-time threshold of 36 units

key_facts: W grade: stays on transcript, does not affect QPA, but does count toward semester unit total
27 enrolled units (after withdrawal) = below 36-unit full-time threshold → part-time status
Going part-time without Dean of Education exception triggers additional academic consequences
P-013 is already on AW — adding a part-time status complication is highly risky
P-013 should consult advisor before withdrawing; dropping to part-time may not be advised
wrong_if_single_domain: Knowing only the withdrawal policy (W grade, no QPA impact) would suggest withdrawal is relatively safe. Only by combining with the unit-count calculation (courses domain) and full-time threshold (policies domain) does the part-time risk become apparent.
common_mistake: Assuming a W grade is always a safe choice because it doesn't hurt QPA; missing that the resulting unit count below 36 triggers a separate part-time policy risk
reasoning_chain: Step 3 (policies): Part-time without Dean approval → additional consequences; especially risky while on AW
Conclusion: P-013 should NOT withdraw unless 6+ units are added elsewhere to stay at 36+; consult advisor immediately
